title: Why CDs Use a 780 nm Infrared Laser to Read Data

scenes.text: A standard audio CD is read by a laser at exactly 780 nm wavelength.
The laser reflects off pits and lands that are just 0.83 µm wide.
A photodiode then converts the reflected light into binary data at 1.41 Mbps.
scenes.query: CD data rate 1.41 megabits per second

scenes.text: Twist: that same 780 nm laser is also used in early DVD players, but with a tighter focus to read 0.4 µm pits.
scenes.query: DVD laser wavelength 780 nm pit size 0.4 micrometer
